title: Transducin-like enhancer of split 3 protects against lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation through DEAD-box helicase 5-activating transcription factor 1-protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit 5A signaling.
authors: Fan, Di; Zhong, Yi; Dong, Yin; Du, Meng; Huang, Kai; Li, Xiaoguang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究TLE3通过DDX5-ATF1轴调控炎症信号通路，涉及蛋白互作但非蛋白质-DNA互作核心，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sepsis consists of life-threatening multi-organ dysfunction caused by an excessive systemic inflammatory response to infection. Therefore, identifying negative regulators of innate inflammation is crucial for treating this condition. OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to understand how transducin-like enhancer of split 3 (TLE3) regulates inflammatory responses. METHODS: We detected Tle3 changes in sepsis patients by analyzing public databases, which were confirmed in septic survivors, septic mouse models, and inflammatory macrophages using Western blotting, qRT-PCR, and immunohistochemistry staining. We investigated the role and mechanism of TLE3 in sepsis by utilizing bone marrow-transplantation (BMT) and adenovirus-infected mice. Furthermore, Protein-Protein Docking, BiFC, LC-MS/MS analysis, CUT & Tag-seq, and CHIP experiments were utilized to disclose the mechanism underlying TLE3 involving macrophage inflammation. RESULTS: In this study, we found that Tle3 transcript is upregulated in peripheral blood samples of sepsis survivors and is decreased in non-survivors, suggesting the critical role of TLE3 in sepsis outcomes. TLE3 is also upregulated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), murine bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), and septic mice. Gain-of- and loss-of-function of TLE3 in LPS-stimulated murine BMDMs, human MDMs, and mouse models of sepsis showed that TLE3 alleviates LPS-induced cytokine production, as well as nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-kappaB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activation in macrophages, which protects against LPS-induced acute systemic inflammation, multi-organ injury, and death caused by sepsis. Mechanistically, upregulated TLE3 interacts with the transcriptional coactivator, DEAD-box helicase 5 (DDX5), promoting its retention in the cytoplasm and ultimately decreasing transcription of the DDX5/ activating transcription factor 1 (ATF1)-targeted gene Ppp2r5a. Furthermore, the TLE3-DDX5-ATF1 axis downregulates PPP2R5A, a negative regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), thereby increasing PP2A activity and promoting the dephosphorylation of NF-kappaB and MAPK. CONCLUSION: Our study shows that TLE3 represents a novel suppressor of LPS-induced inflammatory signaling in macrophages.
abstract_zh: 引言：脓毒症是由感染引发的过度全身炎症反应所导致的危及生命的多器官功能障碍。因此，识别先天炎症的负调控因子对于治疗该疾病至关重要。目的：在本研究中，我们旨在了解转导素样增强子蛋白3（TLE3）如何调控炎症反应。方法：我们通过分析公共数据库检测脓毒症患者中Tle3的变化，并在脓毒症幸存者、脓毒症小鼠模型及炎症巨噬细胞中通过Western blotting、qRT-PCR和免疫组织化学染色进行验证。我们利用骨髓移植（BMT）和腺病毒感染小鼠研究了TLE3在脓毒症中的作用及机制。此外，采用蛋白质-蛋白质对接、BiFC、LC-MS/MS分析、CUT & Tag-seq和CHIP实验来揭示TLE3参与巨噬细胞炎症的机制。结果：在本研究中，我们发现Tle3转录本在脓毒症幸存者的外周血样本中上调，而在非幸存者中下调，提示TLE3在脓毒症结局中的关键作用。TLE3在脂多糖（LPS）刺激的人单核细胞来源巨噬细胞（MDMs）、小鼠骨髓来源巨噬细胞（BMDMs）及脓毒症小鼠中也上调。在LPS刺激的小鼠BMDMs、人MDMs及脓毒症小鼠模型中，TLE3的功能获得和功能丧失实验表明，TLE3减轻LPS诱导的细胞因子产生，以及巨噬细胞中核因子κB（NF-kappaB）和丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）的激活，从而保护免受LPS诱导的急性全身炎症、多器官损伤及脓毒症导致的死亡。机制上，上调的TLE3与转录共激活因子DEAD-box解旋酶5（DDX5）相互作用，促进其滞留于细胞质，最终减少DDX5/激活转录因子1（ATF1）靶基因Ppp2r5a的转录。此外，TLE3-DDX5-ATF1轴下调PPP2R5A（蛋白磷酸酶2A（PP2A）的负调控亚基），从而增加PP2A活性并促进NF-kappaB和MAPK的去磷酸化。结论：我们的研究表明，TLE3是巨噬细胞中LPS诱导炎症信号的新型抑制因子。
